Set up a 2D axisymmetric spray combustion simulation in OpenFOAM using the reactingParcelFoam solver on Linux CLI.
Define the geometry as a cylindrical chamber, 0.2 m in the axial direction (x) and 0.05 m in the radial direction (y), representing a half-radius of a 0.1 m diameter cylinder, with the symmetry axis along y=0.
Generate the mesh using blockMesh with 100 cells in the axial (x) direction and 50 cells in the radial (y) direction.
Apply mesh grading to refine cells near the axis (y=0) and near the injector face (x=0).
Place a cone-type liquid fuel injector centered at the inlet on the axis (x=0, y=0).
Inject n-dodecane (nC12H26) liquid fuel at a total mass flow rate of 0.002 kg/s, initial droplet temperature of 300 K, using a Rosin-Rammler droplet size distribution with a Sauter mean diameter of 50 micrometers.
Set the inlet air boundary condition as velocity U=(10, 0, 0) m/s, temperature 800 K, total pressure 101325 Pa, species mass fractions O2=0.233 and N2=0.767.
Set the outlet boundary condition as totalPressure.
Set the chamber wall boundary condition as noSlip with wall temperature 400 K.
Set the symmetry axis boundary condition as type "axis".
Use the standard k-epsilon turbulence model with turbulence intensity of 5% at the inlet for k and appropriate epsilon initialization.
Model combustion using a two-step global reaction mechanism for n-dodecane oxidation (first step partial oxidation to CO and H2, second step oxidation of CO and H2 to CO2 and H2O).
Use Janaf thermodynamic tables for species enthalpy and heat capacity.
Configure the file structure under constant/sprayCloudProperties, constant/combustionProperties, and constant/reactionSchemes following standard OpenFOAM conventions.
Set the simulation to run until 0.05 s physical time.
Set the Courant number control with maxCo = 0.7 for adaptive time stepping.
Write output fields every 0.001 s.
Run the case from the command line using the standard OpenFOAM execution sequence: blockMesh followed by reactingParcelFoam.
